 2026 Midterm Elections Election Day live blog: How voting went across the country
 Voters headed to the polls amid unprecedented concern about federal interference. Votebeat live-blogged every development.
 By  Natalia Contreras , Hayley Harding , Sasha Hupka , Dion Nissenbaum , Alexander Shur , Carter Walker , Tia Yang , Lauren Aguirre , Elaine Cromie , Sami Edge , Jessica Huseman , Carrie Levine and Nathaniel Rakich  |  November 3, 2026, 11:00am UTC 
 Republish lead-art-block.fullscreen-enter Expand Election workers organize, validate, and tabulate ballots inside Milwaukee’s central ballot processing center on Election Day. (Cullen Granzen for Votebeat) Votebeat is a nonprofit news organization reporting on voting access and election administration across the U.S. Sign up for our free weekly newsletter to get the latest. 
 Election Day 2026 is in the books, and it was generally a smooth day of voting. Although there were some problems at polling places, they were fairly typical for a big election, and fears of federal interference from the Trump administration largely failed to materialize. 
 Votebeat reporters, stationed around the country, covered it all live as it happened. Read our Election Day live blog below.
 The Latest 
 Garlin Gilchrist wins Michigan secretary of state election The Democrat will succeed Jocelyn Benson as Michigan’s top election official and will oversee the 2028 presidential election in the state.
 By  Hayley Harding  |  Today, 7:36am UTC Despite fears, voting ran smoothly across the country Election officials dealt with sporadic, typical problems after months of worrying about what the Trump administration might do. 
 By  Jessica Huseman  |  Today, 4:36am UTC Election Day live blog: How voting went across the country Voters headed to the polls amid unprecedented concern about federal interference.
 By  Natalia Contreras , Hayley Harding and 11 more  |  November 3 Everything you need to know about post-election audits Officials in all 50 states conduct post-election audits to verify that election results are accurate and procedures were followed properly.
 By  Carter Walker  |  November 3 Alaska has a two-Dan problem in key Senate race. But voter confusion seems unlikely to matter. Alaska’s unusual ranked choice voting process makes it less likely confusion over two Dans will matter in a key Senate race.
